newsitem.title: USA: Court okays pact for potential Barney's investors.
newsitem.headline: Court okays pact for potential Barney's investors.

text.p: Barney's Inc said Friday the U.S. Bankruptcy Court signed an order to create a process for soliciting and responding to offers from potential investors.

Barney's said it reached an agreement with Isetan Co and the Official Committee of Unsecured Creditors to create the proposed process. A hearing for pending objections is scheduled June 17, the company said.

Terms call for a negotiation and execution of a definitive investment agreement requiring joint approval by Barney's and the creditors committee. Any agreement must be executed no later than July 25 and filed with the court by July 28.

The selected investor will be paid a commitment fee of $1.5 million if the pact is not finalized. The investor will also be entitled to a fee of $8.5 million, or two percent or less of the proceeds payable under the investment agreement, if Barney's gets and accepts a higher or better offer.
Potential investors must submit a proposal to Barney's investment bankers, the Blackstone Group and the Peter J. Solomon Co, by July 7, Barney's said.
The retailer filed for reorganization under Chapter 11 in January 1996.
